fixes.explanation: That's the group, friend. Festus, who took over after Felix (Acts 24:27), barely gets settled in the province before the chief priests and Jewish leaders present their case against Paul (Acts 25:1-2). Some folks wait for a housewarming gift. These folks brought a legal case.

Not this crowd, friend. The text says the ones presenting a case against Paul are the chief priests and Jewish leaders (Acts 25:2). The apostles and church elders aren't named anywhere in that verse. I'd have loved to see the look on Festus's face if they had shown up, though.
I see why you'd think Rome is involved. But the text names the ones who present the case: the chief priests and Jewish leaders (Acts 25:2). Soldiers aren't listed anywhere in that verse.
That's the man. Festus sits on the judgment seat and orders that Paul be brought in (Acts 25:6). He does it the next day after going down to Caesarea.

Right there. Paul says, "I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried." (Acts 25:10) He also adds that he has done nothing wrong to the Jews, as Festus himself knows very well.

True. Paul says, "If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die." (Acts 25:11) He goes on to say that if there is no truth to their accusations, no one has the right to hand him over to them.
